explainBack.prompt: Why could a colleague see GPT-6 Sol in her model picker while I cannot, even though we both use ChatGPT?
explainBack.response: Because the models were introduced only in ChatGPT Work and Codex, not ordinary Chat, and even within Work the visible model choices depend on the workspace's plan and settings, with a gradual rollout — so two people using different services or workspaces can see different pickers.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P002 places the models in Work and Codex and separate from Chat; P004 notes lists can differ between personal Chat and employer Work; P005 explains plan/workspace settings and gradual rollout.
explainBack.assessment: The article supplies every causal step needed for this answer in ordinary language, so the explain-back succeeds without outside knowledge.

unseenTransfer.prompt: Do the announced lower prices change her Plus subscription, and can she simply switch to Luna in her account?
unseenTransfer.response: No on both counts as stated. The lower figures are per-token API prices charged to developers whose software sends work to the model — a usage meter, not her flat subscription. And Luna was introduced in ChatGPT Work and Codex, separate from ordinary Chat, so she must check her own service's model picker rather than assume the headline applies to her plan.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: P003 defines the API and states the figures are not a subscription price; P002 bounds availability to Work and Codex; P007 gives the check-your-picker procedure; P010 explains per-token usage metering.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this genuinely new scenario completely, showing the service/billing-surface model transfers beyond the cases it discusses.

artifactEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Sol and Luna on September 22. Its release notes place them in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and say they are separate from the models in ordinary Chat.

OpenAI also lists lower API prices. An API is the developer-facing connection that lets software send work to a model and pay for the text it processes. Those figures are not a ChatGPT subscription price.
